7:51 That's the fresh new blood, young soy guys joining construction crews - they get a cold, or have a hangover, and they take 3-4 days off. While I'd smash down 8 steel reserves the night before, chug a tall boy next morning at 5am, and proceed to tear off an entire roof solo.

I think every young guy should for at least a small time join a construction crew - ideally a really shitty broken crew that sucks at communication, overworks you with little pay, includes weirdos with serious issues, and treats you like dogshit because you're a noob laborer. You can't take a sick day off, you're expected to throw up on the job site not at home. If you take a day off because of a hangover, they got a new nickname for you. You'll get bad advice from one foreman, then the other one is screaming you physically yanking you telling you thats the wrong way to do it.
If you're slow, they'll get pissed the fuck off. If you're 1-5min late after lunch or in the morning, they'll yell at you. All for $15/hr or illegally $8/hr


I dont recommend it to anyone with low self esteem - I have barely any, but I'm a weirdo that can somehow push through it... but I attribute those 2 years of construction work to being able to push through 2 illnesses, starting my own online business while helping my father working on his business. While almost everyone around me is watching TV/playing vidya all day even when they're in perfectly good health... But there's something about being forced to do work that you hate. You either 1)learn to resent all work, like some retired copywriters or 2)get conditioned where you can consistently do the required work towards your goals, even when you HATE that work.
